On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-6e6dedfc

## Evidence and rule
Demo 1 input/output: a background-2 grid 23x7 had four 7 markers in the bottom rows at (0-indexed) (18,3), (19,2), (20,3), (21,4). Output is identical except the whole marker motif shifts down one row: markers at rows 19,20,21,22 in the same columns. Test 29x6 had background 0 and a 9-valued pattern spanning rows 14–23. Correct output shifts the complete pattern down one row: preserve first 14 all-zero rows (rows 0–13), then place original rows 14–23 at rows 15–24, while row 14 becomes background. The observed accepted output exactly translated all nonzero cells down one row; dimensions/palette preserved. The 24x6 test with background 0 and color-6 pattern spanning rows 5–11 was solved correctly by shifting the entire pattern down exactly one row: the original rows 5–11 moved to rows 6–12, row 5 became background, all columns were preserved, and dimensions/palette remained unchanged. This further confirms the full-object one-row downward translation. Another accepted test was 8x5, background 0, with color-9 cells at (row,col) (3,0),(4,0),(5,0),(6,1). Correct output shifts every non-background cell down exactly one row, yielding 9s at (4,0),(5,0),(6,0),(7,1), preserving grid dimensions and all columns.

## Additional accepted test evidence
A 10x2 test with background 6 and color-4 cells had rows `[[6,6],[6,6],[6,6],[6,6],[6,4],[4,6],[6,4],[4,4],[6,4],[4,4]]`. The correct output is the entire grid translated down one row: row 0 becomes background, rows 1–9 copy old rows 0–8. The old bottom row is dropped at the boundary. This confirms a rigid one-row downward shift with clipping, including when the pattern touches the bottom.

## Additional accepted test evidence
An 8x5 test with background 7 and a color-5 motif at rows 0–2, columns 3–4 (`[[7,7,7,7,5],[7,7,7,7,5],[7,7,7,5,5]]`) was solved by shifting the entire pattern down exactly one row. Output rows 0–3 contain the original motif translated to rows 1–3; all vacated cells return to 7. The remaining rows stay background. This confirms the rule with a nonzero background and a pattern initially touching the top edge.

## Application
Likely operation: move the entire non-background pattern one row downward, preserving columns and shape; set vacated source cells to background. Infer background from the uniform blank area.
